In the [[2022 Birmingham City Council election|previous council election in 2022]], the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] maintained its control of the council, winning 65 seats. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] formed the main opposition with twenty-two seats, with the [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrats]] on twelve and the [[Green Party of England and Wales|Green Party]] winning two. With the result of two ward counts now expected on 11 May, the results announced to date are [[Reform UK]] 22, [[Green Party of England and Wales|Greens]] 19, [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] 17, [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservatives]] 16, [[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Lib Dems]] 12, [[Independent politician|Independents]] 13. == Background == The [[Local Government Act 1972]] created a two-tier system of metropolitan counties and boroughs covering [[Greater Manchester]], [[Merseyside]], [[South Yorkshire]], [[Tyne and Wear]], the [[West Midlands (county)|West Midlands]], and [[West Yorkshire]] starting in 1974. Birmingham is a district of the West Midlands metropolitan county.{{cite book |title=Local Government in England and Wales: A Guide to the New System |publisher=[[HMSO]] |year=1974 |isbn=0-11-750847-0 |location=London |page=7}} The [[Local Government Act 1985]] abolished the metropolitan county councils, with the metropolitan boroughs individually taking on most of the county-level powers. The [[West Midlands Combined Authority]] was created in 2016 and began electing the [[mayor of the West Midlands]] from 2017, which was given strategic powers covering a region coterminous with the West Midlands metropolitan county.{{cite web |title=CONSTITUTION OF THE WEST MIDLANDS COMBINED AUTHORITY |url=https://www.wmca.org.uk/media/1576/constitution-master-module-2642017.pdf |access-date=4 December 2017}} Since its formation Birmingham City Council has variously been under [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour]] control, [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative]] control and [[no overall control]]. Councillors have predominantly been elected from the Labour Party, Conservative Party and the Liberal Democrats. The council has had an overall Labour majority since the [[2012 Birmingham City Council election|2012 council election]], when they regained control from the Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition that had run the city since 2004.{{Cite news|date=2012-05-04|title=Labour gain control of Birmingham and Dudley councils|language=en-GB|work=BBC News|url=https://www.bbc.com/news/uk-england-birmingham-17922884|access-date=2022-01-20}} John Cotton has led the Labour group on Birmingham City Council since May 2023,{{Cite news |last=Warner |first=Lewis |date=21 May 2023 |title=Labour selects new Birmingham City Council leader, removing Ian Ward |url=https://www.itv.com/news/central/2023-05-21/birmingham-city-council-announce-new-leader |access-date=17 October 2025 |work=ITV News}} with Robert Alden leading the Conservative group,{{Cite news |last=Mayor |first=Rob |date=21 May 2023 |title=Labour Party chooses new Birmingham council leader |url=https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-england-birmingham-65663393 |access-date=2025-10-17 |work=BBC News |language=en-GB}} Roger Harmer leading the Liberal Democrats,{{Cite web |date=9 October 2025 |title=Ed Davey: "Lib Dems offer real change for Birmingham" |url=https://www.birminghamlibdems.org.uk/news/article/ed-davey-lib-dems-offer-real-change-for-birmingham |access-date=17 October 2025 |website=Birmingham Lib Dems |language=en-gb}} Julian Pritchard leading the Greens, Martin Brooks leading the Harborne and Quinton Independents, and Jane Jones leading the Birmingham Independents. == Council composition == ===Prior to the election=== Birmingham City council has been controlled by the [[Labour Party (UK)|Labour Party]] since [[2012 Birmingham City Council election|2012]]. The [[Conservative Party (UK)|Conservative Party]] last held sole control of the council in [[1984 Birmingham City Council election|1984]]. It was under no overall control from [[2003 Birmingham City Council election|2003]] until 2012, run by a Labour-[[Liberal Democrats (UK)|Liberal Democrat]] coalition from 2003 to [[2004 Birmingham City Council election|2004]] and by a Conservative-Liberal Democrat coalition from 2004 to 2012.{{cite news|url=https://www.birminghampost.co.uk/news/local-news/eight-years-conservative-liberal-democrat-rule-3912264|title=Eight years of Conservative-Liberal Democrat rule in Birmingham|work=Birmingham Post|author=Neil Elkes|date=10 May 2012|access-date=25 January 2022}} {| class="wikitable" |- ! colspan="3" | After 2022 election ! colspan="3" | Before 2026 election |- ! colspan="2" | Party !
